company_description: Licious began in 2015 when Abhay Hanjura and Vivek Gupta set out to transform a $55Bn category that was largely unbranded, inconsistent, and untouched by modern food standards. Today, it stands as the country’s most loved, iconic D2C meat brand - elevating everyday meals, setting new benchmarks for safety and freshness, and building an ecosystem where farmers, meat technicians, supply partners and delivery heroes thrive alongside millions of delighted home cooks.

summary: If someone asks me to describe myself in less than 10 seconds, I always use the following quote: “Do not judge me by my success, judge me by how many times I fell down and got back up again.” Nelson Mandela When I chose Science and Mathematics and dreamed of cracking IIT, my father warned me that it was a tough road. Only 2–3% make it. Sixteen-year-old me listened, paused, and said: “I want to be that 3%.” If I could go back in time, I’d hug that kid and thank her for teaching me how to fight for what I truly want. As the adage goes, “Hope is a good thing, may be the best of the things and no good thing ever dies.” I’ve always believed that things work out, especially when it feels like they won’t. And somehow, they always have. Hey! I’m Harshita Mahbubani, a final-year undergraduate at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, and an Incoming Senior Associate at Meesho, something I genuinely never thought I’d crack, until I did. That experience alone reinforced what I’ve seen time and again: faith, effort, and patience have a funny way of aligning. Over the last few years, my journey hasn’t been linear and I’m grateful for that. I’ve explored multiple domains with curiosity and intent. From Supply Chain & Operations at AB InBev, to Growth & Strategy roles at early-stage startups like 10X and PandaMoney, to Product exposure at Hyperpure (Zomato), and marketplace and growth work with Weekday (YC-backed). I’ve tried my hand at business analytics, growth strategy, operations, product thinking, and technical problem-solving, learning that real growth often comes from stepping outside comfort zones. Sometimes confidently, sometimes nervously, and sometimes with a very messy VS Code terminal. What ties all of this together is my interest in business growth, strategy, and operations, backed by analytical thinking and hands-on execution. I enjoy working at the intersection of data, people, and systems, especially in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. Beyond work, I value good conversations. The kind that aren’t just logical, but warm. I love listening to stories, understanding people, exchanging perspectives, and being in spaces that leave you thinking a little deeper or smiling a little wider. Sometimes growth comes from action; sometimes it comes from stillness. And as Krishna says in the Bhagavad Gita, “A man is made by his belief. As he believes, so he is.” So, believe. Things have a way of working out, often better than we imagined. Still learning. Still growing. Still trusting the process. One day at a time.
I have completed my industry training in Vedanta , Rajasthan.

ONGC has a unique distinction of being a company with in-house service capabilities in all areas of Exploration and Production of oil & gas and related oil-field services. ONGC is an integrated energy company with interests in upstream, midstream and downstream sector of the hydrocarbon value chain, renewables, LNG, Power generation, petrochemicals and Value Added Products. ONGC's wholly-owned subsidiary Navratna ONGC Videsh Limited (OVL) is the biggest Indian multinational in the energy space, participating in 32 oil and gas properties in 15 countries. ONGC's subsidiary Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) is a Schedule ‘A’ Miniratna, with a single-location refining capacity of 15 million tons per annum. ONGC subsidiary HPCL is a Maharatna CPSE, and has the second largest share of product pipelines in India with a pipeline network of more than 3370 kms for transportation of petroleum products and a vast marketing network consisting of 14 Zonal offices and 133 Regional Offices.

Oil India Limited (OIL) is a fully integrated Exploration & Production company in the upstream sector, with origin dating back to the glorious year (1889) of oil discovery in India. Oil India Limited which was accorded "MAHARATNA" status on 04th August, 2023, is a state-owned enterprise of the Government of India, under the administrative control of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and is the second largest national oil and gas company in India. Oil India Private Limited was incorporated on 18th February 1959, to expand and develop the newly discovered oil fields of Naharkatiya and Moran in the North-Eastern region of India. In 1961, it became a joint venture company of Government of India and Burmah Oil Company Limited, UK. In 1981, OIL became a wholly owned Government of India enterprise. In FY 2022-23, OIL achieved highest ever Revenue & Profit after Tax (PAT) and also achieved highest ever Natural Gas production during the year. In 2021, OIL acquired additional 54.16% ownership interest in Numaligarh Reìnery Limited (NRL) making OIL the promoter & holding company of NRL. OIL has carved a niche as a leading oil and gas company in the upstream sector with a legacy of hydrocarbon exploration for over six decades and having a share of around 9% of the country’s total crude oil and natural gas production. The company has significant presence across the entire value chain in the hydrocarbon sector, it also produces Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) and transports crude oil and refined petroleum products through cross-country pipelines. The company’s In-Country operations are spread over the areas in the states of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Tripura, Nagaland, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan and offshore areas in Andaman, Kerala-Konkan and KG shallow waters. The company operates a 1157 Km long crude oil pipeline in the Northeast for transportation of crude oil produced by both OIL and ONGCL in the region to feed refineries.
